Project.Name: global-secure-access.xml
Project.Title: Global Secure Access: Identity-Aware Network Access, Ring by Ring

Task.Name: Phase 0 — Decision, architecture and logging
X-N01 Remote-access paths and residual VPN use inventoried (Network & Access N0.1)
Task.Contact: Executive sponsor and CIO (Network & Access Modernization plan)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and CIO (Network & Access Modernization plan) If decided late: The adoption decision has no inventory of the VPN's applications and users to weigh Source: network-access.md

Task.Name: GA0.1 Tenant licenses and onboarding state read; current VPN and SSE functions mapped to the four traffic types
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network security engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-1-decision-and-licensing

Task.Name: D-GA1 Adopt Global Secure Access, per function: Microsoft traffic, internet, private, branch
Task.Contact: Service owner, approved by the authorizing official
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Service owner, approved by the authorizing official Options: Adopt the function; keep the current VPN or SSE for it; run both with each traffic type sent to one service. Recorded with license count, availability quote, compensating controls and exit criteria If decided late: No license count can be ordered, and the Network plan's egress decision (D-N5) can't weigh agent-delivered SASE Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-1-decision-and-licensing

Task.Name: X-ND5 Egress pattern decided for each pilot site (Network & Access D-N5)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering (Network & Access Modernization plan) If decided late: The pilot sites' egress is chosen without knowing whether pattern D, agent-delivered SASE, is available Source: network-access.md

Task.Name: GA0.2 Reference architecture recorded: profiles per population, connector groups, branch pattern; first configuration export with its hash manifest
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network security engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-2-reference-architecture

Task.Name: GA0.3 Network log categories exported by diagnostic setting; Sentinel solution installed; traffic-drop alert on; freshness query clean
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Security operations Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-12-telemetry-and-evidence

Task.Name: GAG0 Gate 0 — Decided per function, logging before any pilot traffic
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Service owner Criteria: Decision record approved per function, with a license count no smaller than the pilot and first ring, an availability quote dated within 30 days and an approver; architecture record and the first configuration export with its hash manifest; the four network log categories reaching the workspace Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#checklist

Task.Name: Phase 1 — Client, Microsoft traffic and the pilot ring
GA1.1 Client packaged as an Intune Win32 app with Learn's commands and detection rule; DoH off; ring 0, the implementing team
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform operations Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-3-client-deployment

Task.Name: GA1.2 Microsoft traffic profile on for ring 0; source IP restoration and Conditional Access signaling on; sign-in share measured
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network security engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-4-microsoft-traffic

Task.Name: GA1.3 Universal tenant restrictions (TRv2) policy approved, tagging on, four-case test recorded
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-8-tenant-restrictions

Task.Name: X-P16 Conditional Access baseline enforced; emergency access accounts vaulted and tested (program P1.6)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform teams (program) If decided late: The compliant network policy has no tested emergency access exclusion, and its report-only run waits Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: GA1.4 Compliant network policy in report-only for 10 business days; break-glass scripts staged
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-7-compliant-network

Task.Name: D-GA3 Turn the compliant network policy On for ring 1
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Service owner Options: On, ring by ring; stay in report-only until every reportOnlyFailure is explained If decided late: Ring 1 runs without the network condition, and its exit waits Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-7-compliant-network

Task.Name: X-P22 Pilot Conditional Access and Intune policies assigned (program P2.2)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform teams (program) If decided late: The pilot cohort's devices can't take the client through Intune, and ring 1 waits Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: GA1.5 Ring 1, fewer than 20 users across roles and sites: client, Microsoft traffic, TRv2 and compliant network for 10 business days; emergency access exclusion tested at ring start
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network security engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-11-coexistence-and-migration

Task.Name: GAG1 Gate 1 — Ring 1 exited on Microsoft traffic
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Service owner Criteria: Every step's Validate passed for ring 0 and break-glass rehearsed; ring 1 for 10 business days with no unresolved Sev-2 ticket; client active on every pilot device; report-only results clean; compliant network On for ring 1 Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-11-coexistence-and-migration

Task.Name: Phase 2 — Private Access and administrative paths
D-GA4 First private applications, and Quick Access as a bridge or per-app from the start
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Service owner Options: Quick Access over the VPN's ranges as a transition, then per-app; per-app from the start for the VPN's most-used applications. DirectAccess can't coexist with Private Access on the same device If decided late: Connector groups can't be sized or placed, and Private Access waits Source: ../books/b09-network/05-sd-wan-sase-and-governed-transport.md#private-access-as-the-vpn-and-directaccess-replacement

Task.Name: GA2.1 Connector groups deployed: two outbound-only connectors per group on Windows Server 2019 or later, TLS 1.2, no inline inspection; private DNS
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform operations Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-6-private-applications

Task.Name: GA2.2 First private applications published per app with their own segments, assignment and Conditional Access, for ring 1; application discovery run
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network security engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-6-private-applications

Task.Name: GA2.3 Administrative hosts behind phishing-resistant policies; domain controller sensors moved from Audit to Enforce for application SPNs
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-10-privileged-protocols

Task.Name: GAG2 Gate 2 — Private applications per app for ring 1
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Service owner Criteria: Each published application has its own segments, group assignment and Conditional Access; Quick Access residual at zero for the moved applications; administrative hosts reachable only under phishing-resistant policies; sensors enforcing Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#checklist

Task.Name: Phase 3 — Internet Access and TLS inspection
D-GA5 Web categories the acceptable-use policy blocks
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Service owner, with the ISSO Options: Block the categories the acceptable-use policy names; decide AI categories separately; every bypass to the exception register If decided late: Security profiles can't be built, and Internet Access waits Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-5-internet-traffic

Task.Name: GA3.1 Security profiles with web content filtering and threat intelligence, linked by Conditional Access for ring 1; the baseline profile last
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network security engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-5-internet-traffic

Task.Name: D-GA6 TLS inspection scope and its certificate authority
Task.Contact: Service owner, approved by the privacy officer
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Service owner, approved by the privacy officer Options: Microsoft-managed certificate; the agency's own intermediate signed by a dedicated CA, not the production PKI. Learn's recommended bypass categories kept, plus those the privacy officer names; no prompt or file content capture without a separate decision If decided late: Inspection can't start, URL and file rules stay unavailable, and Gate 3 waits Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-9-tls-inspection

Task.Name: GA3.2 Inspection intermediate signed; root and intermediate trusted on pilot devices by Intune profile; user notice sent
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: PKI and CA administrators Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-9-tls-inspection

Task.Name: GA3.3 TLS inspection on for the pilot security profile; pinned applications bypassed; failure rate measured
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network security engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-9-tls-inspection

Task.Name: GAG3 Gate 3 — Internet traffic filtered and inspected for ring 1
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO and ISSO Criteria: Security profiles with web filtering and threat intelligence; bypasses in the exception register; TLS inspection from a dedicated CA with the privacy officer's approval and user notice; TLS failure rate under 1% Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#checklist

Task.Name: Phase 4 — Rings 2 and 3, and the VPN's retirement
GA4.1 Client hardening from ring 2: Disable hidden, non-privileged users restricted, help desk elevation path
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform operations Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-3-client-deployment

Task.Name: GA4.2 Ring 2, about 10% of users including one branch, for 20 business days, every function at once
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network security engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-11-coexistence-and-migration

Task.Name: D-GA2 CISA telemetry path for the new access layer, agreed with the TIC delegates
Task.Contact: ISSO, with the agency's TIC delegates
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO, with the agency's TIC delegates Options: CLAW; another path CISA confirms. Agreed before the VPN's web path is retired If decided late: The VPN's web path can't be retired, and Gate 4 waits Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#tic-alignment

Task.Name: X-P31S Program starts rollout wave 1 (start of P3.1)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Platform teams (program) If decided late: Ring 3 has no divisions to follow Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: GA4.3 Ring 3, everyone in scope in waves with the program's divisions; each wave on the ring 2 criteria
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network security engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-11-coexistence-and-migration

Task.Name: GA4.4 VPN routes removed per application after 10 business days with no VPN traffic; the VPN's web path retired; residual VPN use in the exception register
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Network engineering Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#step-11-coexistence-and-migration

Task.Name: GA4.5 Zero Trust Assessment rerun; each network finding's closure chain updated with evidence for every applicable state
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#control-states

Task.Name: GAG4 Gate 4 — Every ring exited, evidence complete
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Service owner, with the ISSO Criteria: Each ring exited on its recorded criteria with measured values; VPN routes removed only after each wave held; CISA telemetry agreed; emergency access exclusion tested at each ring start; evidence package for each finding ready for the assessor (closure is the authorizing official's decision) Source: ../books/guides/global-secure-access-implementation.md#checklist
